questions.article: The Earth Is Moving Toward Its End
questions.q: Reading reports of record heat around the world, how does the article say a person should respond?
options: By waiting for science to solve it
Not quite. The article says: By changing his outlook – the earth’s resources are a preparation ground for the next life, not for entertainment.
By changing his outlook – the earth’s resources are a preparation ground for the next life, not for entertainment
Yes. A changing climate is a silent announcement.
By ignoring the reports
Not quite. The article says: By changing his outlook – the earth’s resources are a preparation ground for the next life, not for entertainment.
By moving to a cooler country
Not quite. The article says: By changing his outlook – the earth’s resources are a preparation ground for the next life, not for entertainment.
questions.rationale: “Changing climate is beyond human control; what is within human control is changing one’s perspective on living on earth.”

questions.article: The Search for True Divine Connection
questions.q: Many who say they believe in God still lack peace of mind. What explanation does the article give?
options: They have not travelled enough
Not quite. The article says: Their belief is ritualistic, without heart and soul, and often mixed with devotion to other things.
They pray too often
Not quite. The article says: Their belief is ritualistic, without heart and soul, and often mixed with devotion to other things.
Their belief is ritualistic, without heart and soul, and often mixed with devotion to other things
Right. True belief is a living connection.
Peace of mind is not meant for believers
Not quite. The article says: Their belief is ritualistic, without heart and soul, and often mixed with devotion to other things.
questions.rationale: “The answer lies in the distinction between true belief in God and the ritualistic belief that is bereft of heart and soul.”

questions.q: A psychologist likened hatred to a corrosive acid. What is the point of the comparison?
options: It can be washed away easily
Not quite. The article says: It does more damage to the vessel that holds it than to its intended target.
It harms only the person hated
Not quite. The article says: It does more damage to the vessel that holds it than to its intended target.
It is useful in small amounts
Not quite. The article says: It does more damage to the vessel that holds it than to its intended target.
It does more damage to the vessel that holds it than to its intended target
Yes. Hatred is a self-inflicted wound.
questions.rationale: “It often causes more damage to the container that holds it than to the intended target.”

questions.q: What way out of the cycle of hatred does the article draw from the Quran?
options: Pardoning and making amends – “Whoever pardons and amends will find his reward with God”
Well read. Forgiveness brings inner peace.
Waiting for the other to apologise first
Not quite. The article says: Pardoning and making amends – “Whoever pardons and amends will find his reward with God”.
Returning the harm in equal measure
Not quite. The article says: Pardoning and making amends – “Whoever pardons and amends will find his reward with God”.
Withdrawing from all relationships
Not quite. The article says: Pardoning and making amends – “Whoever pardons and amends will find his reward with God”.
questions.rationale: “The Quran offers a path out of this cycle, encouraging forgiveness and the pursuit of peace.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, does the birth of a child fail to fill us with wonder?
options: Familiarity – it happens every day, so we take the miracle for granted
Correct. Reflection would bring us face to face with the Creator.
It is hidden from view
Not quite. The article says: Familiarity – it happens every day, so we take the miracle for granted.
It is not really remarkable
Not quite. The article says: Familiarity – it happens every day, so we take the miracle for granted.
Science has explained everything
Not quite. The article says: Familiarity – it happens every day, so we take the miracle for granted.
questions.rationale: “The difference lies in familiarity. We have become so accustomed to the daily occurrence of childbirth that we no longer pause to reflect on its significance.”

questions.q: How does the article divide the task of understanding the Quran’s verses?
options: Modern science for everything
Not quite. The article says: Traditional scholars are the standard for religious commandments; modern research helps with verses about the universe and the self.
Traditional scholars for everything
Not quite. The article says: Traditional scholars are the standard for religious commandments; modern research helps with verses about the universe and the self.
Neither is of any use
Not quite. The article says: Traditional scholars are the standard for religious commandments; modern research helps with verses about the universe and the self.
Traditional scholars are the standard for religious commandments; modern research helps with verses about the universe and the self
Yes. A balanced approach.
questions.rationale: “We should consider traditional scholars as standard in religious matters, but we should also take modern research into account when interpreting scientific verses.”

questions.q: A teacher expelled the young Edison as unfit for school. What did his mother do?
options: She accepted the teacher’s judgement
Not quite. The article says: She convinced him his disability was a challenge he could overcome, and made his education her mission.
She sent him to work in a factory
Not quite. The article says: She convinced him his disability was a challenge he could overcome, and made his education her mission.
She moved to another country
Not quite. The article says: She convinced him his disability was a challenge he could overcome, and made his education her mission.
She convinced him his disability was a challenge he could overcome, and made his education her mission
Right. A mother’s constructive role.
questions.rationale: “She instilled in Edison the belief that he was not a disabled child but that his disability was a challenge he could overcome.”

questions.q: What does the article say the real choice in life is?
options: Not between problems and no problems, but between different kinds of difficulty – so one must learn to live and build with them
Yes. “With every hardship there is ease.”
Between wealth and poverty
Not quite. The article says: Not between problems and no problems, but between different kinds of difficulty – so one must learn to live and build with them.
Between work and rest
Not quite. The article says: Not between problems and no problems, but between different kinds of difficulty – so one must learn to live and build with them.
Between a hard life and an easy one
Not quite. The article says: Not between problems and no problems, but between different kinds of difficulty – so one must learn to live and build with them.
questions.rationale: “The choice is not between a life with problems and a life without problems but between different kinds of difficulties.”

questions.article: The Virtue of Returning Good for Evil
questions.q: Trees take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen. What moral example does the article see in this?
options: Turning what is harmful into benefit – answering harm with good
Exactly. “Repel evil with what is better.”
Taking more than one gives
Not quite. The article says: Turning what is harmful into benefit – answering harm with good.
Keeping apart from others
Not quite. The article says: Turning what is harmful into benefit – answering harm with good.
Giving back exactly what one receives
Not quite. The article says: Turning what is harmful into benefit – answering harm with good.
questions.rationale: “Trees do not give back what they receive; they improve the world around them by transforming what is harmful into something beneficial.”

questions.q: The article gathers the last words of several of history’s most powerful men. What does it conclude from them?
options: Death should not be thought about
Not quite. The article says: The insight that comes at death comes too late – the time to remember death is before it arrives.
Great men die content
Not quite. The article says: The insight that comes at death comes too late – the time to remember death is before it arrives.
Power brings lasting peace
Not quite. The article says: The insight that comes at death comes too late – the time to remember death is before it arrives.
The insight that comes at death comes too late – the time to remember death is before it arrives
Well reasoned. Worldly glory then seems futile.
questions.rationale: “There is no point in remembering death when it comes; the time to remember death is before it arrives.”
